proposals.idea: An unseen foreground point-mass lens at low Galactic latitude is crossing a reddened background source, achromatically magnifying its light. Its accelerating approach explains the simultaneous g- and r-band excess over the Type Ia forecast while the g-r colour stays near 1.25 mag.
proposals.name: Galactic microlens magnification
proposals.predicts: It predicts a continued achromatic steepening rise to a single symmetric peak around closest approach followed by a mirror-image decline at unchanged colour, not the colour-evolving turnover of a supernova.

proposals.idea: An unseen foreground point mass in the Galactic plane is crossing the line of sight to a distant red star, gravitationally magnifying it instead of an explosion brightening. The constant red colour and accelerating rise common to both bands over about 25 days trace the shrinking impact parameter of the lens.
proposals.name: Galactic microlensing alignment
proposals.predicts: It predicts an achromatic rise to a smooth peak followed by a mirror-image decline on the same timescale at constant g-r colour, not the colour evolution and asymmetric decay of a Type Ia supernova.

proposals.idea: At galactic latitude -5 degrees, the reference template likely blends a bright red neighbour in this crowded field, while a per-band zero-point and subtraction drift leaks progressively more of its flux into the photometric aperture. This additive residual is much stronger in r than g, mimicking an accelerating, very red transient brightening instead of a supernova photosphere.
proposals.name: Crowded template calibration drift
proposals.predicts: Future fluxes will follow a roughly linear per-band drift with seeing-correlated, non-PSF or offset residuals in the stamps, rather than showing a supernova peak and radioactive decline, and will change if the template or calibration is rebuilt.
